source: Mason and Singh (2016) Categorization of Mechanics Problems by Students in Large Introductory Physics Courses (table reproducing Chi 1981 percentages)
finding: Their Table 1 lists Chi 1981 category use by 8 novices and 8 experts next to 3 large classes. This gives the Chi numbers second-hand, but from a table, not prose. The original Chi paper is paywalled (Wiley returns 403) and was not opened.
numbers: Chi novices (8 intro students): angular motion 87.5%, springs 75%, center of mass 62.5%, inclined planes 50%, kinetic energy 50%, pulleys 37.5%, Newton 2 0%, energy 0%. Chi experts (8 physics grad students): Newton 2 75%, energy 75%, angular motion (non-circular) 75%, momentum 75%, circular motion 62.5%, center of mass 62.5%, statics 50%. Version II (Chi problems only, 109 algebra-based students): energy 31%, Newton 2 18%, linear kinematics 44%, angular/circular 59%.
quote: introductory students were sensitive to the contexts or surface features of the problems
limits: Secondary source for Chi. Chi problems not named in the paper were discarded, so M&S reused only 7. Chi sample is 8 vs 8.
agent_relevance: Chi's headline rests on 16 people. Treat the effect as direction only.

source: Rodionov et al. (2026) Reasoning Shift: How Context Silently Shortens LLM Reasoning (COLM 2026)
finding: Current reasoning models (Qwen3.5-27B, gpt-oss-120b, Gemini 3 Flash Preview, Kimi K2 Thinking, Gemma 4 31B) think much less when a problem arrives with long irrelevant context, as a subtask, or after other turns. Accuracy falls a little on IMOAnswerBench and the fall sits on medium and hard items. Forcing extra checks ('Wait') only partly repairs it.
numbers: IMOAnswerBench accuracy drop 12% (Qwen3.5-27B), 9% (gpt-oss-120b), 15% (Gemini 3 Flash), 9% (Kimi K2) under Subtask and Long Input. Reasoning length falls up to 74%; a few hundred distractor tokens cut Qwen3.5-27B reasoning by 18%, larger inserts by 50%. 50 runs per task on 30 items for the difficulty split.
quote: reasoning models tend to produce much shorter reasoning traces (up to 74%)
limits: Context is long and irrelevant, not a GSM-NoOp style single clause. Not a test of typing or restating.
agent_relevance: Gap 3 in part: distractor harm persists in 2026 reasoning models and the mechanism is less self-checking. A strip-the-context step may help by restoring the clean-problem condition; untested here.

source: Rajeev et al. (2025) Cats Confuse Reasoning LLM: Query-Agnostic Adversarial Triggers for Reasoning Models (COLM 2025)
finding: Appending one irrelevant sentence to a math problem raises the error rate of strong reasoning models by a multiple and also lengthens answers. Triggers were found on a cheap proxy model (DeepSeek V3) and transferred.
numbers: DeepSeek R1: random error rate 1.50%, with triggers 4.50% (3.0x). R1-distill-Qwen-32B: 8.00% (2.83x). On 1,000 GSM8K items, combined trigger factors were 5.14x (Qwen3-30B-A3B), 3.61x (Phi-4-reasoning), 1.15x (QwQ-32B), 7.21x (Mistral-Small-24B). Response length doubled in at least 16% of cases.
quote: appending Interesting fact: cats sleep most of their lives to any math problem leads to more than doubling the chances
limits: Relative multiples on very low base rates (R1 goes from 1.5% to 4.5%, an absolute +3 points). Triggers were optimised adversarially, so this is a worst case, not natural distractors.
agent_relevance: Do not quote '300%' alone. Absolute harm to strong reasoners is small on easy math but cost rises. Supports a cheap drop-irrelevant-text guard, but the size is a few points, not tens.

source: Nazi, Dipta, Kar (2026) DAGGER: Distractor-Aware Graph Generation for Executable Reasoning in Math Problems
finding: On a Bangla distractor benchmark (DistractMath-BN on MGSM and MSVAMP), 5-shot CoT models lose up to 41 points and reasoning models still lose 14-20 points while using 5x more tokens. A fine-tuned Gemma-3 that writes a typed graph with distractor nodes marked and then executes it loses 12.0-14.4 points with about 359 tokens. This is the closest test of restate-and-strip.
numbers: CoT Qwen2.5-3B 53.7% to 13.0% on MSVAMP (-40.7). Qwen3-8B reasoning: 71.4% weighted accuracy, drop 14.2-19.9, 3,128 tokens per problem. DAGGER Gemma-3 12B GRPO: 69.4%, 359 tokens, 89% fewer tokens. Related-entity distractors give 46-94% error. Distractor-node annotations: +2.9 (4B) and +5.0 (12B) on the distractor split, +0.1/+0.6 on original.
quote: enforcing structured intermediate representations can improve robustness and inference efficiency
limits: Fine-tuned, not prompt-only. Bangla, 3B-12B models. GPT-4.1 comparison (DAGGER beat CoT, PoT, GoT) exact numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: Best evidence found that an explicit typed representation with marked irrelevant parts beats plain CoT at lower token count. Still needs a prompt-only version on frontier models.

source: Chen et al. (2025) Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: o1-like models spend far more tokens on trivial items with little accuracy gain. The first solution round is usually already right, so extra rounds are mostly redundant. This is the cost side of forcing extra steps on easy items.
numbers: 1,953% more tokens than conventional models on 'what is 2 plus 3?'. In more than 92% of cases the first round of solutions was correct; the first round was under 60% of total tokens (QwQ-32B-Preview on ASDIV: 287 tokens, 38.7% of the response). 13 solutions for one trivial question.
quote: excessive computational resources are allocated for simple problems with minimal benefit
limits: Tests o1-like models (QwQ, R1), not S2 typing. Easy sets: ASDIV, GSM8K, MATH500.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: when surface and structure agree (easy items) extra deliberation buys almost nothing, so S2 should be gated by difficulty or a quick uncertainty check.

source: Sprague et al. (2025) To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning (ICLR 2025)
finding: Meta-analysis of over 100 papers plus own runs on 20 datasets and 14 models. CoT gains are concentrated in math and symbolic tasks. On MMLU, CoT is almost identical to direct answers unless the question or response has an equals sign. Splitting plan and execution shows most of CoT's gain is in execution; a symbolic solver beats CoT at execution.
numbers: Top three categories improved by 14.2, 12.3 and 6.9 points on average; average on those with CoT 56.9 vs 45.5 without. MMLU and MMLU Pro gains come from the math slices.
quote: CoT gives strong performance benefits primarily on tasks involving math or logic
limits: Zero-shot CoT versus direct answer, not S2 typing versus CoT. Models are 2024 (Llama 3.1, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5).
agent_relevance: Put the cost into the solve/execute step (code, solver) rather than a longer representation step. Expect typing gains on math and physics, not on knowledge items.

source: DeepSeek-AI (2026 v2) DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via RL
finding: The authors state R1 is prompt-sensitive and that few-shot prompting consistently lowers its accuracy. They recommend describing the problem directly in a zero-shot setting.
numbers: No number given for the few-shot drop in the passage read.
quote: Few-shot prompting consistently degrades its performance.
limits: A single statement, no table, in the prompting note. One model family.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: scaffolds built from worked examples (Step-Back exemplars, skill exemplars) may hurt current reasoning models. Test zero-shot typing instructions separately from example-based ones.

source: Zhou et al. (2024) Self-Discover: LLMs Self-Compose Reasoning Structures
finding: A structure-choosing step gives large gains on a weaker model and smaller ones on GPT-4 for maths, and it is cheaper than self-consistency.
numbers: BBH / T4D / MATH. PaLM 2-L: CoT 60/40/42, Self-Discover 67/69/50.5. GPT-4: CoT 75/52/71, Self-Discover 81/85/73. GPT-4 gain over CoT: +6 BBH, +33 T4D, +2 MATH. Claims 10-40x fewer inference calls than CoT-Self-Consistency.
limits: Equal tokens against a single CoT is not tested; select/adapt/implement calls add tokens. GPT-4 (2023), not a current reasoning model.
agent_relevance: Partial answer to gap 1: on a strong non-reasoning model the structure gain over CoT shrinks on maths (+2) but stays large on agent-style T4D. Gain depends on the task, not only model strength.

source: Didolkar et al. (2024) Metacognitive Capabilities of LLMs: An Exploration in Mathematical Problem Solving (GSM8K, with embedding-retrieval baseline)
finding: Skill-labelled exemplars beat an embedding-similarity retrieval baseline (Retrieval-RSD) on GSM8K with GPT-3.5-Turbo, and beat CoT only slightly on GPT-4. All use 8-shot prompts, so context size is about equal.
numbers: GSM8K GPT-3.5-Turbo: Retrieval-RSD 76.8 vs skill-based 82.03 (+5.2). GPT-4-0613: CoT 93.00, CoT+Random 92.87, skill-based 94.31 (+1.3), skill-based maj@5 95.38. MATH GPT-4: CoT 42.2, Complex CoT 50.30, topic-based 50.31, skill-based 53.88.
limits: Skill labels made by GPT-4, coarse; agreement with human labels not measured. The Retrieval-RSD row is from GPT-3.5 only. Temperature 1.0.
agent_relevance: Nearest evidence on gap 8: skill/structure labels beat surface-embedding retrieval by about 5 points at equal shots on a weaker model; on a strong model about 1 point on GSM8K and 3.5 on MATH.

source: Didolkar et al. (2024) skill-label transfer to Mixtral 8x7B (Table 5, MATH)
finding: Labels made by GPT-4 still help a different model, and topic labels do not. The paper says GPT-4 labels gave the strongest in-context result compared with labels from GPT-3.5-Turbo and Mixtral, so label quality depends on the annotator.
numbers: Mixtral MATH: CoT maj@4 28.4; single sample topic-based 26.14 vs skill-based 28.44; with maj@4 topic-based 30.75 vs skill-based 32.44. Label-annotator comparison is in appendix 10.4, not read.
limits: No human structural labels to compare against, so agreement (gap 6) is not measured.
agent_relevance: Check label agreement before using type labels for retrieval. Gap 6 stays open for code.

source: Levy, Bogin, Berant (2023) Diverse Demonstrations Improve In-context Compositional Generalization (ACL 2023)
finding: Choosing examples by similarity to the input works on i.i.d. splits but fails when the output needs unseen structures. Choosing a set that covers the structures of the target output (Cover-LS) raises accuracy a lot. Structure coverage beats surface similarity mainly when similar examples are not enough.
numbers: Up to +23 absolute points, e.g. 50.3 to 73.5 on SMCalFlow-CS, against a similarity-retrieval baseline with Codex; fewer demonstrations needed. Datasets: SMCalFlow-CS, GeoQuery, COVR-10.
limits: Semantic parsing with Codex, not open reasoning. Needs a structure predictor for the target.
agent_relevance: Gaps 7 and 8: structure-coverage retrieval pays when a new case differs structurally; on in-distribution items similarity is enough. Memory should mix both and gate by novelty.

source: Lanham et al. (2023) Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
finding: Inserting a mistake into a chain of thought or truncating it changes the final answer a lot on some tasks and not at all on others. Larger and more capable models rely less on the stated reasoning. A written step is not automatically what drives the answer.
numbers: No single number; effect varies by task and model size across 8 tasks.
quote: As models become larger and more capable, they produce less faithful reasoning on most tasks
limits: 2023 models, no type-label manipulation. Indirect evidence on gap 4.
agent_relevance: Forced-wrong-label tests are needed: a strong model may ignore a wrong S2 label, which would show the label is not causal there.

source: Chen et al. (2025) Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think
finding: Claude 3.7 Sonnet and DeepSeek R1 used planted hints in their answers but said so in the reasoning under 20% of the time in most settings, and less on harder tasks. Outcome-based RL raised faithfulness at first then plateaued.
numbers: Models used hints at least 1% of the time in most settings; verbalised them under 20% in most settings.
quote: often verbalize it less than 20% of the time
limits: Hints are answer cues, not type labels. Indirect for gap 4.
agent_relevance: A type label the model writes may not be the real cause of its answer. Use externally forced or code-checked labels to test causality.

source: Mizrahi et al. (2024) State of What Art? A Call for Multi-Prompt LLM Evaluation (TACL)
finding: Meaning-preserving instruction paraphrases change both absolute scores and model rankings across 39 tasks and 20 LLMs (6.5M instances). Rank agreement across templates is only medium on most tasks.
numbers: Kendall's W across templates roughly .71 to .91 on the tasks listed (logical deduction .776, navigate .873, language identification .913); 175+ verified paraphrases.
limits: Instruction wording only, not item wording; 2023-2024 models. Sorting or typing tasks were not the focus.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: typing or sorting results from one prompt wording are not safe. Run each item under 2-3 paraphrases and report agreement. The 76-point Sclar swing is a maximum over formats, not typical.

source: Liu et al. (2025) Mind Your Step (by Step): Chain-of-Thought can Reduce Performance on Tasks where Thinking Makes Humans Worse (ICML 2025)
finding: Forcing verbal reasoning lowers accuracy on tasks where humans also do worse when they verbalise, such as implicit statistical learning. o1-preview dropped heavily against GPT-4o.
numbers: Artificial grammar learning subset: GPT-4o 94.00% vs o1-preview 57.70%, a 36.3 point absolute drop (p<0.0001). Other tasks mixed.
limits: o1-preview could not be run without reasoning, so GPT-4o served as the no-CoT comparison; not a same-model contrast.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: explicit S2 can hurt where recognition works better than explanation (pattern tasks). Gate S2 off where fast recognition is reliable.

source: Li et al. (2024) GSM-Plus: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating the Robustness of LLMs as Mathematical Problem Solvers
finding: Eight perturbation types on GSM8K (including distractor insertion and critical thinking) across 25 LLMs and 4 prompting methods. All models drop. Larger models are less hurt by distractor insertion.
limits: 2024 models. Per-type distractor numbers sit in a figure not extracted.
agent_relevance: Distractor harm shrinks with model strength but does not vanish; consistent with a small guard step for strong models.

source: Webb, Holyoak, Lu (2023) Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models (Gick-Holyoak radiation problem replication in GPT-3)
finding: GPT-3 shows the Gick and Holyoak pattern: with unrelated distractor stories it fell back to the same solution as for the radiation problem alone, and when prompted to consider the earlier stories it picked the analogous general story and gave the convergence solution. No Gick-Holyoak percentages appear in the text read.
numbers: Qualitative in the main text; details in supplementary sections S5.4 and S5.5, not opened.
limits: The original Gick and Holyoak percentages were not found in any open source this session.
agent_relevance: A model can use the structural match once pointed at it, as in Gick-Holyoak. Supports an explicit look-for-a-structural-match step rather than hoping for spontaneous retrieval.

source: Null-result record: search for 2025-2026 LLM card-sort replications, code-task type-label agreement, and reasoning-model Step-Back tests
finding: The WebSearch budget was exhausted and the arXiv, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar search endpoints returned 429 during this run. No new paper was found for gap 2 (multi-model sorting), gap 6 (code type labels vs human labels), or an exact reasoning-model Step-Back test (gap 1). Absence here is not evidence of absence.
limits: Search failure, not a literature negative. Only fetch-by-id was possible.
